# Stack changes and restack them automatically

## Intent

An agent that builds a second change on top of an unlanded first one should not have to rebase by hand every time the first one moves. This package lets changes depend on one another as a stack, and makes the hub keep every change of a stack built on the change below it: when a lower change gets a new version or lands, the hub rebases the changes above it, records the result as a new version, and, when the rebase cannot be done, says so on the change with a conflict report and moves nothing.

## Goals

- A change's `depends_on` is set by the caller (at open or by `PATCH`) or by the hub from the commit graph at open and on every new version, and `dependants` lists the `draft` and `open` changes directly above.
- An explicit `depends_on` that names an unknown change, a change with another target branch, a change that is not `draft` or `open`, or a change that would close a cycle is refused with `400 invalid_dependency` and changes nothing.
- A stack deeper than `[changes].max_stack_depth` (default 20) is still recorded; the change past the limit carries `needs_restack: true` with `restack_reason: "stack_too_deep"`.
- A new version of a change with dependants causes, in the background and without client action, a `restack` version of every change above it, bottom first.
- Landing a change rebases each direct dependant onto the landed commit, clears its `depends_on`, and restacks the changes further up in turn.
- A restack that conflicts moves no branch for that change or any change above it, sets `needs_restack: true`, `restack_reason: "conflict"`, `mergeable: "conflict"` and a conflict report, and emits `parley.change.conflict` once.
- With the workspace setting `changes.auto_restack` false, the hub only sets `needs_restack` with `restack_reason: "auto_restack_off"`.
- `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/restack` does the same rebase on demand and answers `200` with `restacked` or `up_to_date`, or `409 rebase_conflict` with the conflict report.
- `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/stack` returns the whole stack, bottom first.
- A restack that was pending when the hub stopped runs after the next start.
- `parley change restack` and `parley change stack` drive the two routes.

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. The change record, its store, version recording and the read routes arrive with package 22 in `internal/change/`; the `PATCH`, abandon and restore routes and the mergeability check with package 23 in the same directory; the rebase, ref compare-and-swap and ancestry queries with `internal/gitrepo/`; the event component with package 52 in `internal/event/`; the router and error envelope with package 02 in `internal/server/`; the CLI root, HTTP client and output rules with package 09 in `internal/cli/`.

This package adds to `internal/change/`: the stack link and depth rule (`stack.go`), the restack operation and its durable pending records (`restack.go`, `restack_queue.go`), the manual restack handler (`restack_handler.go`) and the stack route (`stack_handler.go`), each with its test file beside it; to `internal/config/` the key `[changes].max_stack_depth`; and to `internal/cli/change.go` the commands `restack` and `stack`. The tasks do not edit the files of packages 22 and 23: they implement and register the interfaces those packages declare, `StackLinker` (`internal/change/collaborators.go`, package 22) and `Restacker` (`internal/change/lifecycle.go`, package 23), and call their setters, their version recording and the function that stores `mergeable` with its conflict report. ## Requirements

All routes are under `/api/v1/workspaces/:slug`, where `:slug` is the workspace of the change's target branch.

### The stack link (§7.3.3)

A change depends on another when its commits sit on top of that change's commits. `depends_on` holds the number of the change directly below, or `null`. `dependants` holds the numbers of the `draft` and `open` changes whose `depends_on` is this change, ascending.

The automatic rule runs when a change is opened without an explicit `depends_on` and on every new version of a change, whatever created the version. Among the other `draft` or `open` changes of the same workspace with the same target branch, the hub looks for those whose current `head_sha` is a proper ancestor of the new head and takes the nearest one (the fewest commits between it and the new head). That change becomes `depends_on`, and the version's `base_sha` is its head. When there is none, `depends_on` is cleared and `base_sha` is the merge base with the target branch. A change whose head equals the new head is not below it. Changes in state `landed` or `abandoned`, and changes with another target branch, are never candidates. Cycles cannot arise from this rule. A dependant that is force-pushed directly onto the target therefore loses its link (§7.10).

A dependent change's `base_sha` is the head of the change below; its diff, stats and paths cover only its own commits. All changes of a stack have the same target branch; they may come from different source workspaces (the target workspace and its forks).

### Explicit `depends_on` (§7.3.3, §7.5 `PATCH`)

`depends_on` in the body of `POST …/changes` and of `PATCH …/changes/:number` sets the link by hand. The value is refused with `400`, `error_type: invalid_dependency`, and nothing is changed, when it names: a change number that does not exist in the workspace; the change itself or a change whose own stack already contains this change (a cycle); a change with a different target branch; a change that is not `draft` or `open`. `PATCH` with `depends_on: null` clears the link and sets `base_sha` to the merge base with the target.

After an accepted explicit link, when the lower change's head is an ancestor of the change's head the change's `base_sha`, `stats` and `paths` are recomputed against that head. When it is not, the change is not yet built on the change below: with `changes.auto_restack` true a restack of it is recorded as pending and runs in the background; with it false the change gets `needs_restack: true`, `restack_reason: "auto_restack_off"`.

### Stack depth (§7.3.3, §7.9)

The depth of a change is the number of changes in the chain of `depends_on` links from it down to a change with none, itself included. `[changes].max_stack_depth` (integer, default 20) is the deepest allowed stack; a value below 1 stops the server at start with exit status 1 and one error line on stderr. A version or an explicit link that puts a change at a depth above the limit is still recorded with its link, and the change gets `needs_restack: true`, `restack_reason: "stack_too_deep"`. A change at exactly the limit is not flagged. The hub does not restack a too-deep change, or anything above it, on its own. The flag is recomputed whenever the change's link or a link below it changes, and is cleared once the depth is at or under the limit.

### Restack on a new version below (CHG-FR-030, CHG-FR-033)

When a change that has dependants gets a new version, the hub records one pending restack per direct dependant in the same transaction as the version. The push or commit that caused the version is answered without waiting. A background worker then, for each dependant: reads the dependant's source branch head; replays the dependant's own commits (those after its `base_sha` up to its head) onto the new head of the change below; moves the dependant's source branch to the result with a compare-and-swap; and records a version of kind `restack` whose `created_by.actor_type` is `system`, whose `base_sha` is the new head below and whose `session_id` is that of the version it replaces. A restack that changes no patch is `patch_equivalent_to` the previous version. The hub emits `parley.change.version` with `kind: "restack"` and then `parley.change.restack` with `onto_sha` (the new head below) and `trigger: "version"`, both with actor `system`.

Because the restack is itself a new version of the dependant, it causes the restack of that change's dependants in the same way, so the work continues up the stack, bottom first.

A dependant whose head already has the new head below as an ancestor is left alone: no version, no event; a `needs_restack` flag with reason `conflict` or `auto_restack_off` is cleared.

The restack moves the source branch on the hub; the author's local branch is then behind, and a `git pull --rebase` or a fetch of `refs/parley/changes/<number>/<version>` brings it up to date. If the source branch moved between the hub reading it and the compare-and-swap, the restack is tried again on the new head, at most 5 times in one run. After the fifth lost compare-and-swap a background restack stays pending and nothing is changed.

If the lower change was force-pushed to an unrelated head, its dependants are restacked onto it by the same replay of their own commits; this may conflict (§7.10).

### Restack on landing below (CHG-FR-031)

When a change lands, the after-landing step (package 25, LAND-FR-017) calls this package with the landed change and the landed commit on the target. For each direct dependant the hub clears `depends_on` and records a pending restack onto the landed commit. The worker replays the dependant's own commits onto the landed commit, moves the source branch with a compare-and-swap and records a `restack` version whose `base_sha` is the landed commit; the events are as above with `trigger: "land"`. Changes further up keep their `depends_on` and are restacked in turn by the rule of the previous section.

When a change with dependants is abandoned with `dependants=reparent` (package 23, CHG-FR-022), package 23 gives each direct dependant the abandoned change's `depends_on` as its own and asks this package, through `Restacker` and inside the abandon's transaction, to restack it; it is restacked onto the head of that change, or onto the current head of the target branch when there is none, without the abandoned change's commits; the events carry `trigger: "abandon"`.

### Restack failure (CHG-FR-032, §8.3.3)

If the replay conflicts, no branch moves for that change, and no restack is started for any change above it. The change gets `needs_restack: true`, `restack_reason: "conflict"`, `mergeable: "conflict"` and `conflict` set to the conflict report. `parley.change.conflict` is emitted with actor `system` and metadata `files` (the conflicted paths) and `needs_restack: true`. The event is not emitted again while the change stays in conflict. `mergeable`, the report and the event are written by the storing function of package 23, called with the pair of the change's head and the commit replayed onto, so that the background check of that package and a restack never announce one conflict twice.

After a successful restack `mergeable` needs no write here: the `restack` version sets it to `unknown` and package 23 computes it for the new head against the head the change now sits on. When a flag is cleared without a new version (an `up_to_date` manual restack), this package asks package 23's trigger to compute it again.

The conflict report has the members `target_sha` (the commit the work was being replayed onto), `head_sha` (the dependant's head), `base_sha` (the commit the work was based on), `commit_sha` (the first commit that did not apply), `files`, `landed_changes` and `change`. Each file entry has `path`, `kind` (`content`, `add_add`, `modify_delete`, `delete_modify`, `rename`, `mode`, `binary` or `submodule`), `base`, `ours`, `theirs` (each `{sha, mode, path}` or `null` where the file does not exist on that side; `ours` is the commit replayed onto, `theirs` the change) and `landed_by`. In this package `landed_changes` is `[]`, every `landed_by` is `[]` and `change` is `null`.

A later version of the change whose head has the commit it must sit on (the current head of the change below, or the landed commit) as an ancestor clears `needs_restack` and `restack_reason`. A later version that leaves the change with no `depends_on` by the automatic rule, while the change was linked, clears them too, because there is no longer a change below.

### `changes.auto_restack` (CHG-FR-035)

`changes.auto_restack` is a workspace setting of the target workspace, default true. While it is false, a new version below and a landing below record no pending restack and move no branch: each direct dependant that is not built on the new head gets `needs_restack: true`, `restack_reason: "auto_restack_off"`. On landing, `depends_on` is still cleared. The rebase is left to the manual call.

### Manual restack (CHG-FR-034, §7.5)

`POST …/changes/:number/restack` with an optional body `{"session_id"?: string, "resolutions"?: [...]}` does the same operation on demand and answers synchronously. It needs `changes:write`, and the caller must be the change's author, have write access to the target workspace, or use the admin token (CHG-FR-020); a caller who can read the change but is none of these gets `403 forbidden`; a PAT without the scope gets `403 insufficient_scope`; an unknown number gets `404`, `error_type: change_not_found`.

The commit to sit on is the current head of the change named by `depends_on`, or the current head of the target branch when `depends_on` is `null`.

- The change's head already has that commit as an ancestor: `200 {"status": "up_to_date", "change": <change object>}`. No version and no event; a `needs_restack` flag with reason `conflict` or `auto_restack_off` is cleared.
- Otherwise the change's own commits are replayed and the source branch is moved: `200 {"status": "restacked", "change": <change object>}`. A version of kind `restack` is recorded whose `created_by` is the caller and whose `session_id` is the body's `session_id`, or that of the previous version when the body has none. `parley.change.version` and then `parley.change.restack` (`onto_sha`, `trigger: "manual"`) are emitted with the caller as actor. `needs_restack` is cleared unless its reason is `stack_too_deep`.
- A version guard is registered and refuses the version the replay would record (package 29: a path-scoped token and a file outside its `paths`): the guard's answer, `403`, `error_type: path_not_allowed` with the path. The guard is asked after the replay is computed and before the source branch moves, with the caller's credential and the base and head of the version; nothing is changed. A restack the hub makes on its own does not ask it.
- The replay conflicts: `409`, `error_type: rebase_conflict`, with the conflict report in the envelope's `details`. The change is left as in "Restack failure".
- The change is `landed` or `abandoned`: `409`, `error_type: change_closed`.
- The change has no `depends_on` and its target branch no longer exists: `400`, `error_type: target_not_found`.
- `session_id` fails the session-linking rule of §14: `400`, `error_type: unknown_session`; nothing is changed.
- The source branch moved under the hub five times in a row: `409`, `error_type: ref_moved`, with `current_sha` in `details`; nothing is changed.

A `resolutions` member is ignored here; package 26 gives it its meaning.

### Durability (§7.7, NFR-013)

A pending restack is a record in the transactional store, written in the transaction of the event that caused it. There is at most one per change; recording another for the same change replaces it. It is removed when the restack ends (restacked, up to date, conflict, or the change is no longer `draft` or `open`). At start the hub runs every pending restack it finds, so that one that was pending at shutdown is run after the next start. Restacks are not retried with backoff.

When the `git` command fails for a reason other than a conflict (it cannot be started, it exits with an error, the repository cannot be read), a background restack changes nothing, keeps its pending record and is logged; the record is run again at the next start or when another restack is recorded for the same change. The manual call answers `500`, `error_type: internal`, and changes nothing. The worker never stops the server process.

### The stack route (§7.5)

`GET …/changes/:number/stack` needs `changes:read` and read access to the target workspace. It answers `200 {"target_branch": string, "changes": [<summary>…]}`. The list holds the chain of `depends_on` links below the change, the change itself, and every `draft` or `open` change above it through `dependants`, ordered by depth from the bottom and then by number. Each summary has `number`, `title`, `state`, `version`, `head_sha`, `mergeable`, `needs_restack`, `restack_reason` and `landing` as `{"status": …}`. A change with no link and no dependants answers with a list of one. An unknown number answers `404 change_not_found`.

### CLI (§7.6)

- `parley change restack <slug> <number>` calls `POST …/changes/:number/restack` with an empty JSON object, prints the response on stdout and exits 0. A conflict prints the envelope with the conflict report on stderr and exits 1.
- `parley change stack <slug> <number>` calls `GET …/changes/:number/stack`, prints the response and exits 0.

### End-to-end flows

1. An agent pushes three branches with stock git, each one commit on top of the previous, and opens a change for each. The hub links them: 2 depends on 1, 3 depends on 2. The agent amends the bottom branch and pushes it. The push is answered; shortly after, changes 2 and 3 each have a new version of kind `restack` created by `system`, their source branches sit on the new heads below, and the stack route lists the three bottom first with `needs_restack: false`.
2. An agent has two stacked changes that edit the same line. It pushes a new version of the lower one that rewrites that line. The hub's restack of the upper change conflicts: the upper branch does not move, the change shows `needs_restack: true`, `restack_reason: "conflict"` and a conflict report. `parley change restack` prints the `rebase_conflict` envelope and exits 1. The agent rebases the upper branch onto the new lower head locally and pushes it; the flag is cleared and `parley change stack` shows both changes with `needs_restack: false`.

## Design Decisions

1. **Language, store and git.** Go; the store is embedded SQLite behind `internal/store`; git operations run the `git` binary through `internal/gitrepo`; no git library. These are the project-wide decisions.
2. **Tests.** Standard `testing` package, table-driven; handlers with `net/http/httptest`; repositories created with `git init` in `t.TempDir()`.
3. **A change's own commits are `base_sha..head_sha`.** Every restack replays exactly the commits after the change's recorded `base_sha`, whatever happened to the change below. This is what makes "patch replay" onto an unrelated head (§7.10) and the rebase without an abandoned change's commits the same operation.
4. **Automatic rule: proper ancestor, nearest first, lowest number on a tie.** The PRD says "nearest ancestor"; two changes may share a head, so the tie goes to the lower number, and a change with the same head as the new version is never its parent, which keeps cycles impossible.
5. **An explicit `depends_on` at open wins over the automatic rule for that version; every later version runs the automatic rule.** The PRD says the link is set "explicitly, at open or by `PATCH`; or automatically at open and on every new version" and does not rank them.
6. **`invalid_dependency` applies at open too.** The PRD lists it only under `PATCH`; the same four causes are refused the same way in `POST …/changes`.
7. **An explicit link to a change the caller's commits do not sit on schedules a restack** (trigger `manual`, version created by `system`), or sets `auto_restack_off` when the setting is false. The PRD does not say what happens; this keeps the definition of `needs_restack` true without a new reason value.
8. **A too-deep change keeps its link.** The PRD says the version "is still recorded" and the flag is set; the link is recorded too so that the stack route shows the real chain. Depth is counted downward from each change, so only the changes past the limit are flagged. An explicit link that exceeds the limit is flagged, not refused, because `invalid_dependency` does not list depth. A manual restack of a too-deep change rebases it and leaves the flag.
9. **`[changes].max_stack_depth` below 1 fails the start.** The PRD gives no bounds; a stack needs at least one change.
10. **`depends_on` is cleared whenever the change below lands**, including when `auto_restack` is false or the restack conflicts. A link is only ever to a `draft` or `open` change; the change remembers the landed commit as the commit it must sit on until it does.
11. **Clearing the flag.** `needs_restack` with reason `conflict` or `auto_restack_off` is cleared by a version that has the required commit as an ancestor (CHG-FR-032), and also when the automatic rule removes the link of a linked change, since the definition of the flag needs a change below.
12. **Compare-and-swap retries are capped at 5 per run.** The PRD says the restack "is retried on the new head" without a bound. A background restack that loses five times stays pending; the manual call answers `409 ref_moved` with `current_sha`, the type §6 defines for a lost compare-and-swap.
13. **Who made a restack version.** Hub restacks are `system` (§7.3.2). A manual restack's version is created by the caller, as §14.8 gives the caller as the actor of a manual restack's event. A restack version keeps the `session_id` of the version it replaces unless the manual call's body names one.
14. **A manual restack that conflicts leaves the same state as an automatic one** (flag, report, one `parley.change.conflict`), because CHG-FR-034 calls it "the same operation".
15. **Manual restack with a missing target branch is `400 target_not_found`**, the type and status CHG-FR-003 uses for the same fact.
16. **Conflict report content.** The report is the type `ConflictReport` of `internal/gitrepo`, declared by package 20 and returned by the compare route, the rebase of package 21 and the mergeability check of package 23 alike. This package fills `target_sha`, `head_sha`, `base_sha`, `commit_sha` and the file entries from the rebase result of `internal/gitrepo`, and leaves `landed_changes` and `landed_by` empty ("Empty when unknown", §8.3.3) and `change` null. Package 26 fills the rest.
17. **`resolutions` is ignored here.** Unknown members are ignored by PLAT-FR-017; package 26 extends the same handler.
18. **The stack route returns the chain below, the change, and all changes above.** The PRD says "the whole stack the change is part of"; where a change has several dependants all are listed, ordered by depth and then number.
19. **Wiring to packages built earlier and later.** Package 22 calls `LinkVersion` of its `StackLinker` at open and on every version and package 23's `PATCH` calls `SetDependsOn`; package 23's abandon calls `Restacker`. This package implements both interfaces and registers them; it specifies what they do, and those packages specify nothing about `depends_on` beyond handing it over (package 22 validates only that it is a positive integer; package 23 relinks dependants on reparent). The fields `depends_on`, `needs_restack`, `restack_reason` and the derived `dependants` are package 22's and are written through its setters. The landing trigger is one function in `internal/change/`, registered as an after-landing hook of package 25 as decision 23 says; this package's tests call it directly.
20. **A restack that fails without a conflict stays pending** and is run again at the next start or at the next restack recorded for the same change; the manual call answers `500 internal`. The PRD says restacks are durable and not retried with backoff, and names no failure other than a conflict.
21. **One pending restack per change.** A newer one replaces the older, because the commit to sit on is the newest one.
22. **Profile: full.** Ten requirements and two end-to-end flows.
23. **The landing entry point reaches `internal/land` through `internal/hub` (with package 25).** Package 25 declares the after-landing hook list in `internal/land/hooks.go`; a hook is called with the landed attempt (its workspace, the update of the target branch and the session) and, per landed change, its number, its source workspace and branch and its landed commit. `internal/hub/change.go` registers an adapter of that shape which calls the entry point once per landed change with the workspace, the number and that change's landed commit. `internal/change` imports nothing of `internal/land`, and package 25 is not a dependency of this package; a hook failure never changes the land.
24. **The version guard of the manual restack (with package 29).** This package declares `VersionGuard` with `RegisterVersionGuard` in `internal/change/restack_handler.go`. The manual restack calls it after the replay is computed and before the compare-and-swap of the source branch, with the caller's credential (type, id and `paths`) and the base and head of the version to record; a refusal is answered unchanged (`403 path_not_allowed` with the path) and leaves the change, its branch and its flags as they were. Background restacks, whose actor is `system`, do not call it. Without a registered guard every version passes. Package 29 registers the guard.
25. **Wiring is in `internal/hub/change.go`**, beside the wiring of packages 22 and 23.

## Dependencies

- Package 23 `change_lifecycle_and_mergeability` (draft): the `PATCH` and abandon routes that call this package through `StackLinker` and `Restacker`, the caller rule of CHG-FR-020, and the function that stores `mergeable` with its conflict report. Through it: package 22 (change record, version recording, read routes), packages 18 and 21 (`internal/gitrepo` rebase and compare-and-swap, git push), package 11 (workspace settings), package 07 (access rule), package 52 (events), packages 02 and 09 (HTTP and CLI conventions).
- By registration, not as dependencies: package 25 `optimistic_landing` (its after-landing hook list, filled from `internal/hub/change.go`) and package 29 `auto_land_revert_and_path_limits` (which registers the version guard).
- The `git` command, 2.38 or later, at run time.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task.
- **Change**: The unit of work: a proposal to add the commits of a source branch to a target branch, with a number, a title, an intent, versions and a state.
- **Version**: One head of a change's source branch. Every push, API commit or restack that moves the source creates a new version. Old versions stay fetchable.
- **Stack**: Changes linked by `depends_on`, lowest first.
- **Restack**: The hub rebasing a dependent change onto the new head of the change below it, or onto the target once that change has landed.
- **Landing**: Adding a change's commits to its target branch: a server-side rebase followed by a compare-and-swap of the target ref.
- **Conflict report**: The structured description of why a rebase could not be done: files, kinds, and the landed changes involved.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number.
- **Dependant**: A `draft` or `open` change whose `depends_on` names the change in question.
- **Pending restack**: The stored record that a change must be rebased onto a given commit, kept until the restack ends.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Automatic stack link

**Rationale:** An agent that pushes one branch on top of another expects the hub to see the stack without being told.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN package 22 calls LinkVersion of its StackLinker interface, which this package implements, for a version it records for a draft or open change that has no explicit depends_on for that version, and the current head of at least one other draft or open change of the same workspace with the same target branch is a proper ancestor of the new head, THE parleyd SHALL set the change's depends_on to the nearest such change (the one with the fewest commits between its head and the new head) and the version's base_sha to that change's head, both through the setters of package 22
   → the change object has depends_on equal to the lower change's number and base_sha equal to the lower change's head_sha
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/stack_test.go, a table over {B opened on top of A; C opened on top of B on top of A (C must link to B, not A); A in state draft and B open; A's source in the target workspace and B's source in a fork of it; B at version 1 and B at a later pushed version}: record the version through the version recording of package 22; assert change.depends_on == number of the nearest lower change; assert change.base_sha == that change's head_sha
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN a version is recorded for a draft or open change and no other draft or open change with the same target branch has a current head that is a proper ancestor of the new head, THE parleyd SHALL clear the change's depends_on and set the version's base_sha to the merge base of the new head and the target branch
   → the change object has depends_on null and base_sha equal to the merge base with the target branch
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/stack_test.go, a table over {a first change on main; B that depended on A and is then force-pushed directly onto main}: record the version; assert change.depends_on == null; assert change.base_sha == mergeBase(head, main); for the second row assert A.dependants does not contain B
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any version it records, never choose as depends_on a change that is landed or abandoned, a change with another target branch, a change of another workspace, or a change whose head equals the new head, and choose the lowest number when two candidates share the nearest head
   → depends_on names only a draft or open change of the same workspace and target branch whose head is a proper ancestor of the change's head
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/stack_test.go, a table over the lower candidate {landed, abandoned, open with target branch release while the new change targets main, open in another workspace whose repository holds the same commits, open with the same head as the new version}: record a version on top of the candidate's head; assert change.depends_on == null. One more row: changes 3 and 5 are open with the same head, a new change is pushed on top of it; assert depends_on == 3
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] THE parleyd SHALL for any link it sets or clears, store it through the depends_on setter of package 22, so that the dependants package 22 derives for every change list exactly the draft and open changes whose depends_on is that change
   → dependants on the change object (rendered by package 22): array of integers, ascending, [] when there is none; this package keeps no second list of dependants
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/stack_test.go: A with B and C both opened on top of A, and D on top of B; assert A.dependants == [B, C]; assert B.dependants == [D]; assert D.dependants == []; abandon C through the store; assert A.dependants == [B]
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] THE parleyd SHALL for any dependent change, compute stats and paths of the current version from the commits after base_sha only, so that they cover the change's own commits and none of the change below
   → stats.commits equals the number of commits after the lower change's head; paths lists only files those commits touch
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/stack_test.go: A has 2 commits touching a.txt; B is opened on top of A with 1 commit touching b.txt; assert B.stats.commits == 1; assert B.stats.files_changed == 1; assert B.paths == ['b.txt']
   ```

### REQ-2: Explicit depends_on

**Rationale:** A caller sometimes knows the order of its changes before the commit graph shows it, and must be told when the order it asks for is impossible.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a caller sends depends_on with the number of a draft or open change of the same workspace and target branch, in the body of POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes or of PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes/:number, and the link would not form a cycle, THE parleyd SHALL set the change's depends_on to that number and, when the lower change's head is an ancestor of the change's head, set base_sha to that head and recompute stats and paths against it
   → HTTP 201 (open) or 200 (PATCH) with the change object carrying depends_on equal to the given number
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/stack_test.go with httptest, a table over {POST …/changes with depends_on: A for a branch built on A; PATCH B with depends_on: A where B is built on A's head and its link was cleared before by PATCH depends_on: null; PATCH B with depends_on: A where B is built on main only}: assert status == 201 or 200; assert json.depends_on == A.number; where B is built on A assert json.base_sha == A.head_sha; assert GET A .dependants contains B
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF the depends_on sent at open or by PATCH names a change number that does not exist in the workspace, the change itself, a change whose own stack contains the change (a cycle), a change with a different target branch, or a change that is not draft or open, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and change nothing: no change is created at open, and no field of an existing change is modified
   → HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_dependency, returned as an error from LinkVersion (open) or SetDependsOn (the PATCH of package 23), whose transaction is rolled back; the stored change (or the count of changes, at open) is unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/stack_test.go with httptest, a table over the value {999 (unknown), the change's own number, a change that depends on this one directly, a change that depends on this one through one change in between, a change targeting release, a landed change, an abandoned change} and the route {PATCH; POST …/changes for the rows that apply at open}: r = request; assert r.status == 400; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_dependency'; assert the stored change equals its state before the request, or count(changes) is unchanged; one row sends title together with the invalid depends_on and asserts the title is unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN a caller sends PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes/:number with depends_on null on a change that has a depends_on, THE parleyd SHALL clear the link, set base_sha to the merge base of the change's head and the target branch, and recompute stats and paths against it
   → HTTP 200 with the change object carrying depends_on null; the former lower change's dependants no longer lists the change
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/stack_test.go with httptest: B depends on A; r = PATCH B {depends_on: null}; assert r.status == 200; assert r.json.depends_on == null; assert r.json.base_sha == mergeBase(B.head, main); assert r.json.stats.commits == commits of A plus commits of B; assert GET A .dependants == []
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] WHEN an explicit depends_on is accepted, the lower change's head is not an ancestor of the change's head, and the target workspace's setting changes.auto_restack is true, THE parleyd SHALL record a pending restack of the change onto the lower change's head in the same transaction as the link, and let the background worker run it with trigger manual
   → after the worker runs, the change has a new version of kind restack with created_by.actor_type system and base_sha equal to the lower change's head; parley.change.restack carries trigger manual
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: A and B are both built on main and touch different files; PATCH B {depends_on: A}; assert a pending restack for B exists; runPending(); v = latest version of B; assert v.kind == 'restack'; assert v.base_sha == A.head_sha; assert isAncestor(A.head_sha, B.head_sha); assert last event of type parley.change.restack has metadata.trigger == 'manual'
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] WHILE the target workspace's setting changes.auto_restack is false and an explicit depends_on is accepted whose lower change's head is not an ancestor of the change's head, THE parleyd SHALL record no pending restack, move no branch, and set needs_restack to true with restack_reason auto_restack_off on the change
   → the change object has needs_restack true and restack_reason auto_restack_off; its version number and source branch head are unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: as the check above but with changes.auto_restack false: r = PATCH B {depends_on: A}; assert r.json.needs_restack == true; assert r.json.restack_reason == 'auto_restack_off'; assert no pending restack exists; assert B.version and head(B.source) are unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] WHEN a change is opened with an explicit depends_on, and a later version of it is recorded, THE parleyd SHALL keep the explicit link for version 1 whatever the commit graph says, and apply the automatic rule to the later version
   → after the open, depends_on is the given number; after the later version, depends_on is what the automatic rule yields
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   - setup: changes.auto_restack is false, so that no restack moves B between the two steps
   ```
   in internal/change/stack_test.go: A and X are open on main; B's branch is built on X's head; open B with depends_on: A; assert B.depends_on == A.number; push one more commit to B's branch (still on X); assert B.depends_on == X.number
   ```

### REQ-3: Stack depth limit

**Rationale:** An unbounded chain makes every push at the bottom cost a rebase per change above; the limit caps that cost without losing a pushed head.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a recorded version or an accepted explicit depends_on puts a change at a depth (the number of changes in its chain of depends_on links down to a change with none, itself included) above [changes].max_stack_depth, THE parleyd SHALL record the version and the link all the same, and set needs_restack to true with restack_reason stack_too_deep on that change, leaving every change at or under the limit unflagged
   → the change object past the limit has needs_restack true and restack_reason stack_too_deep, its version is recorded and its depends_on is set; a change at exactly the limit has needs_restack false
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/stack_test.go, a table over {max_stack_depth 3 with a chain of 5 opened bottom first: changes 1-3 unflagged, 4 and 5 flagged; the key absent from configuration with a chain of 21: change 20 unflagged, change 21 flagged; max_stack_depth 3 and PATCH depends_on that attaches a change on top of a chain of 3: flagged, answered 200}: for each change assert needs_restack and restack_reason as listed; assert every change has a recorded version 1 and the depends_on of the change below
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHILE a change has restack_reason stack_too_deep, THE parleyd SHALL start no restack of that change, and none of any change above it, when a change below it gets a new version or lands
   → the too-deep change's source branch head and version number are unchanged, and no pending restack exists for it
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: max_stack_depth 2, chain A, B, C (C flagged); push a new version of A; runPending(); assert latest version of B has kind 'restack'; assert C.version == 1; assert head(C.source) is unchanged; assert no pending restack exists for C; assert C.restack_reason == 'stack_too_deep'
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] WHEN a link of a too-deep change or of a change below it changes so that the change's depth is at or under [changes].max_stack_depth, THE parleyd SHALL clear needs_restack and restack_reason on it and, when its head does not have the head of the change below as an ancestor, record a pending restack for it (or set restack_reason auto_restack_off when changes.auto_restack is false)
   → the change object has needs_restack false and restack_reason null once it sits on the head below
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: max_stack_depth 2, chain A, B, C (C flagged); push a new version of A and runPending() (B restacked, C untouched); move main to a landed commit that holds A's patch, mark A landed through the store, call the landing entry point for A with a landed commit on main and runPending(); assert B.depends_on == null; assert C.needs_restack == false; assert C.restack_reason == null; assert latest version of C has kind 'restack' and base_sha == B.head_sha
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF the configuration sets [changes].max_stack_depth to a value below 1, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse to start
   → the server process exits with status 1 and writes one error line naming changes.max_stack_depth to stderr; it never listens
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/config/config_test.go, a table over max_stack_depth {0, -1}: err = Load(file); assert err != nil; assert err message contains 'changes.max_stack_depth'. And over {1, 20, 500}: assert err == nil and cfg.Changes.MaxStackDepth == the value; with the key absent assert the value is 20
   ```

### REQ-4: Restack on a new version below

**Rationale:** The agent that amends the bottom of a stack should find the changes above it rebased without doing anything.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a change that has direct dependants gets a new version while the target workspace's setting changes.auto_restack is true, THE parleyd SHALL record one pending restack per direct dependant in the same transaction as the version, and answer the push or commit that caused the version without running any of them
   → when the triggering request has been answered, a pending restack exists for each direct dependant and each dependant's source branch head and version number are still what they were
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_queue_test.go: A with dependants B and C (both on A); record a new version of A with the worker stopped; assert pending restacks == {B, C}; assert B.version == 1 and C.version == 1; assert head(B.source) and head(C.source) are unchanged; and with a store that fails the pending write, assert the version of A is not recorded either
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN the worker runs a pending restack for a dependant whose head does not have the new head of the change below as an ancestor, and the replay of the dependant's commits applies, THE parleyd SHALL move the dependant's source branch with a compare-and-swap to the replayed commits and record a version of kind restack with created_by.actor_type system, base_sha equal to the new head below, the session_id of the version it replaces, and patch_equivalent_to naming the previous version when the diff against its base is identical; clear needs_restack and remove the pending record
   → the dependant has a new version {kind: restack, created_by.actor_type: system, base_sha: <new head below>}; its source branch head equals that version's head_sha, which has the new head below as its ancestor; needs_restack is false
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: B (1 commit touching b.txt, session s1) depends on A; amend A (touching a.txt) and record its version; runPending(); v = latest version of B; assert v.number == 2; assert v.kind == 'restack'; assert v.created_by.actor_type == 'system'; assert v.base_sha == A.head_sha; assert v.session_id == 's1'; assert v.patch_equivalent_to == 1; assert head(B.source) == v.head_sha; assert isAncestor(A.head_sha, v.head_sha); assert B.needs_restack == false; assert no pending restack exists
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN the hub records a restack version on its own after a new version below, THE parleyd SHALL emit parley.change.version with kind restack and then parley.change.restack with onto_sha set to the new head below and trigger version, both with actor system and with ref, version and head_sha of the dependant in the metadata
   → two events in this order for the dependant: parley.change.version {kind: restack}, parley.change.restack {onto_sha, trigger: version}; actor system; resource_type change; resource_id the change number
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go, in the scenario of the check above with the event log of package 52: evs = events for resource B after the amend; assert types(evs) == ['parley.change.version', 'parley.change.restack']; assert evs[0].metadata.kind == 'restack'; assert evs[1].metadata.onto_sha == A.head_sha; assert evs[1].metadata.trigger == 'version'; assert both have actor system, metadata.version == 2 and metadata.head_sha == B.head_sha
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] WHEN a restack version is recorded for a change that itself has dependants, THE parleyd SHALL restack those dependants in the same way, so that the work continues up the stack bottom first
   → every change above the amended one ends with a restack version whose base_sha is the current head of the change directly below it
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: chain A, B, C, D, each one commit on a file of its own; amend A; runPending() until no pending restack is left; for X in (B, C, D): assert latest version of X has kind 'restack' and base_sha == head_sha of the change below; assert the restack events were written in the order B, C, D
   ```
1. [REQ-4.5] WHEN the worker runs a pending restack for a dependant whose head already has the new head of the change below as an ancestor, THE parleyd SHALL record no version, emit no event, clear a needs_restack flag whose reason is conflict or auto_restack_off, and remove the pending record
   → the dependant's version number and source branch head are unchanged; no parley.change.version or parley.change.restack event is written for it
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: B depends on A; the author rebases B onto A's amended head and pushes it before the worker runs; runPending(); assert B.version == 2 and its kind is 'push'; assert no event of type parley.change.restack exists for B; assert no pending restack exists
   ```
1. [REQ-4.6] WHEN the dependant's source branch moved between the hub reading its head and the compare-and-swap, THE parleyd SHALL run the restack again on the new head, at most 5 attempts in one run
   → the restack version's head contains the commit that was pushed in between, replayed onto the new head below
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go, with a hook that pushes one more commit to B's source branch after the first read of its head: amend A; runPending(); v = latest version of B; assert v.kind == 'restack'; assert the commits after v.base_sha have the subjects of B's original commit and of the commit pushed in between; assert head(B.source) == v.head_sha
   ```
1. [REQ-4.7] IF the compare-and-swap of a background restack is lost 5 times in one run, THEN THE parleyd SHALL stop the run, change nothing and keep the pending record
   → no restack version and no parley.change.restack event exist for the dependant; its needs_restack is unchanged; the pending record is still present
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go, with a hook that moves B's source branch before every compare-and-swap: amend A; runPending(); assert the rebase ran exactly 5 times; assert no version of kind 'restack' exists for B; assert a pending restack for B exists; assert no parley.change.restack event exists for B
   ```
1. [REQ-4.8] THE parleyd SHALL for any restack, replay exactly the commits after the change's base_sha up to its head, in order, including when the change below was force-pushed to a head unrelated to its previous one
   → the new version has the same number of commits after its base_sha as the old one, with the same subjects and the same patches
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: B has 3 commits on top of A; A's branch is force-pushed to a new commit created from main that shares none of A's old commits and touches other files; runPending(); v = latest version of B; assert count(v.base_sha..v.head_sha) == 3; assert their subjects equal B's original subjects in order; assert git patch-id of each equals the original's; assert none of A's old commits is an ancestor of v.head_sha
   ```

### REQ-5: Restack on landing and on reparenting

**Rationale:** When the bottom of a stack lands or is abandoned, the next change must sit on what replaced it, not on commits that are no longer a change.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN the landing entry point is called for a change that landed with a landed commit on the target, and changes.auto_restack is true, THE parleyd SHALL in one transaction, clear depends_on of each direct dependant and record a pending restack of it onto the landed commit; record nothing when the landed change has no dependants
   → each direct dependant has depends_on null and a pending restack whose onto commit is the landed commit
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_queue_test.go: chain A, B, C; move main to a landed commit L that holds A's patch and mark A landed through the store; OnLanded(A, L) with the worker stopped; assert B.depends_on == null; assert pending restacks == {B onto L}; assert C.depends_on == B.number. Second row: OnLanded for a change without dependants; assert no pending restack exists
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] WHEN the worker runs a pending restack onto a landed commit and the replay of the dependant's commits applies, THE parleyd SHALL move the dependant's source branch with a compare-and-swap, record a restack version whose base_sha is the landed commit, and emit parley.change.version and then parley.change.restack with onto_sha equal to the landed commit and trigger land
   → the dependant has depends_on null and a new version {kind: restack, base_sha: <landed commit>}; parley.change.restack carries trigger land
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go, continuing the scenario above: runPending(); v = latest version of B; assert v.kind == 'restack'; assert v.base_sha == L; assert count(v.base_sha..v.head_sha) == number of B's own commits; assert the last parley.change.restack event for B has metadata.onto_sha == L and metadata.trigger == 'land'
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] WHEN a direct dependant of a landed change has been restacked and has dependants of its own, THE parleyd SHALL keep the depends_on of the changes further up and restack them in turn onto the new head of the change directly below
   → a change two levels above the landed one still has depends_on naming the change directly below it, and a restack version whose base_sha is that change's new head
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go, continuing the scenario above until no pending restack is left: assert C.depends_on == B.number; v = latest version of C; assert v.kind == 'restack'; assert v.base_sha == B.head_sha; assert isAncestor(L, v.head_sha)
   ```
1. [REQ-5.4] WHEN the abandon of package 23, called with dependants=reparent, has set a direct dependant's depends_on to the abandoned change's depends_on and asks the Restacker interface, which this package implements, to restack that dependant with trigger abandon, THE parleyd SHALL record a pending restack of the dependant in the transaction it is given and restack it onto the head of the change it now depends on, or onto the current head of the target branch when there is none, replaying only the dependant's own commits; emit parley.change.restack with trigger abandon
   → each dependant's new version has none of the abandoned change's commits among its ancestors; its depends_on is the one package 23 set (the abandoned change's former depends_on) and this package does not write it; parley.change.restack carries trigger abandon; with changes.auto_restack false the dependant gets needs_restack true with restack_reason auto_restack_off and no pending restack
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go, a table over {chain A, B, C with B abandoned: C.depends_on == A.number and C's restack version has base_sha == A.head_sha; chain A, B with A abandoned: B.depends_on == null and B's restack version has base_sha == head(main)}: abandon through the abandon route of package 23 with dependants=reparent; runPending(); assert the listed values; assert no commit of the abandoned change is an ancestor of the dependant's head; assert the last parley.change.restack event has metadata.trigger == 'abandon'
   ```

### REQ-6: Restack failure

**Rationale:** A conflict must be visible on the change as data and must never leave a branch half rebased.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] IF the replay of a change's commits in a restack conflicts, THEN THE parleyd SHALL move no branch for that change, set needs_restack to true with restack_reason conflict, set mergeable to conflict and conflict to the conflict report through the storing function of package 23, for the pair of the change's head and the commit replayed onto, and remove the pending record
   → the change object has needs_restack true, restack_reason conflict, mergeable conflict and a non-null conflict; its version number and source branch head are unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: A and B (on A) both edit line 1 of f.txt; amend A to rewrite line 1 again; runPending(); assert B.needs_restack == true; assert B.restack_reason == 'conflict'; assert B.mergeable == 'conflict'; assert B.conflict != null; assert B.version == 1; assert head(B.source) is unchanged; assert no pending restack exists; assert no worktree or temporary ref of the rebase is left in the repository
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] IF a restack conflicts for a change that has dependants, THEN THE parleyd SHALL start no restack for any change above it
   → every change above keeps its version number, its source branch head and needs_restack false; no pending restack exists for it
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: chain A, B, C where the amend of A conflicts with B and C touches another file; runPending(); assert C.version == 1; assert head(C.source) is unchanged; assert C.needs_restack == false; assert C.depends_on == B.number; assert no pending restack exists
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] WHEN a restack of a change fails with a conflict and the change was not already in conflict, THE parleyd SHALL have the storing function of package 23 emit parley.change.conflict with actor system and metadata files (the conflicted paths) and needs_restack true, by setting the flag before calling it
   → one event parley.change.conflict for the change with metadata {files: [paths], needs_restack: true, ref, version, head_sha}
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go, in the first scenario of this requirement: evs = events of type parley.change.conflict for B; assert len(evs) == 1; assert evs[0].metadata.files == ['f.txt']; assert evs[0].metadata.needs_restack == true; assert evs[0].actor is system; assert evs[0].metadata.version == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-6.4] IF a restack fails with a conflict for a change that already has needs_restack true with restack_reason conflict, THEN THE parleyd SHALL replace the stored conflict report with the new one through the storing function of package 23, which emits no further parley.change.conflict event
   → the count of parley.change.conflict events for the change stays 1; conflict.target_sha is the newest head below
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch

   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go, continuing the first scenario: amend A a second time, again conflicting; runPending(); assert count(events of type parley.change.conflict for B) == 1; assert B.conflict.target_sha == A.head_sha
   ```
1. [REQ-6.5] THE parleyd SHALL for any conflict it reports from a restack, use the one report type ConflictReport of internal/gitrepo that package 20 declares, and give it the members target_sha (the commit replayed onto), head_sha (the change's head), base_sha (the change's base), commit_sha (the first commit that did not apply), files, landed_changes as [] and change as null, where each file entry has path, kind (one of content, add_add, modify_delete, delete_modify, rename, mode, binary, submodule), base, ours and theirs (each {sha, mode, path}, or null where the file does not exist on that side) and landed_by as []
   → a JSON object with exactly the members target_sha, head_sha, base_sha, commit_sha, files, landed_changes, change; every sha is 40 hexadecimal characters
   Check: unit

### REQ-7: Workspaces with automatic restack off

**Rationale:** Some teams want every branch move to be asked for; the hub then only says which changes are behind.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHILE the target workspace's setting changes.auto_restack is false and a change with direct dependants gets a new version, THE parleyd SHALL record no pending restack, move no branch, and set needs_restack to true with restack_reason auto_restack_off on each direct dependant whose head does not have the new head as an ancestor
   → each such dependant has needs_restack true and restack_reason auto_restack_off with its version number and source branch head unchanged; a dependant already on the new head is not flagged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: changes.auto_restack false; A with dependants B and C; amend A by adding a commit on top (so that B, built on the old head, is behind) and then push C rebased onto A's new head; assert B.needs_restack == true; assert B.restack_reason == 'auto_restack_off'; assert B.version == 1; assert head(B.source) is unchanged; assert C.needs_restack == false; assert no pending restack exists; assert no parley.change.restack event exists
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] WHILE the target workspace's setting changes.auto_restack is false and the landing entry point is called for a change with direct dependants, THE parleyd SHALL clear depends_on of each direct dependant, set needs_restack to true with restack_reason auto_restack_off on it, record no pending restack and move no branch
   → each direct dependant has depends_on null, needs_restack true and restack_reason auto_restack_off; its source branch head is unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_test.go: changes.auto_restack false; chain A, B; land A as L through the store and OnLanded(A, L); assert B.depends_on == null; assert B.needs_restack == true; assert B.restack_reason == 'auto_restack_off'; assert head(B.source) is unchanged; assert no pending restack exists
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] WHEN a caller sends the manual restack for a change that has restack_reason auto_restack_off, THE parleyd SHALL do the rebase the automatic restack would have done and clear the flag
   → HTTP 200 with status restacked and a change object with needs_restack false and restack_reason null
   Check: same as REQ-8.1

### REQ-8: Manual restack

**Rationale:** An agent must be able to ask for the rebase itself and get the outcome in the same call, including the conflict as data.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN the change's author, a caller with write access to the target workspace or the admin token sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/restack, with no body or a JSON object, for a draft or open change whose head does not have as an ancestor the commit it must sit on (the current head of the change named by depends_on, or the current head of the target branch when depends_on is null), and the replay applies, THE parleyd SHALL replay the change's own commits onto that commit, move the source branch with a compare-and-swap, record a version of kind restack created by the caller with the body's session_id (or the previous version's when the body has none), emit parley.change.version and then parley.change.restack with trigger manual and the caller as actor, and clear needs_restack unless its reason is stack_too_deep
   → HTTP 200 with body {status: "restacked", change: <change object>}; change.version is one higher, change.base_sha is the commit sat on, change.needs_restack is false
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch

1. [REQ-8.2] WHEN a permitted caller sends the manual restack for a draft or open change whose head already has the commit it must sit on as an ancestor, THE parleyd SHALL record no version, emit no event, and clear a needs_restack flag whose reason is conflict or auto_restack_off, asking the mergeability trigger of package 23 to compute mergeable again when a flag was cleared
   → HTTP 200 with body {status: "up_to_date", change: <change object>}; change.version is unchanged

1. [REQ-8.3] IF the replay of a manual restack conflicts, THEN THE parleyd SHALL move no branch, leave the change with needs_restack true, restack_reason conflict, mergeable conflict and the conflict report, emit parley.change.conflict unless the change was already in conflict, and answer with the report
   → HTTP 409 with error_type rebase_conflict and the conflict report as the envelope's details object; the source branch head and the version number are unchanged

### REQ-9: Durable restacks

**Rationale:** A restack the hub owes must not be forgotten because the hub stopped between a push and its background work.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-9.1] WHEN the hub starts and the store holds pending restacks, THE parleyd SHALL run every one of them
   → after the start, each change that had a pending restack has its restack version (or its conflict state) and no pending record remains
   Check: integration
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_queue_test.go: open a real store in t.TempDir(); chain A, B; record a new version of A with the worker stopped; close the store; reopen it and start the worker as the server start does; wait until no pending restack is left; assert latest version of B has kind 'restack' and base_sha == A.head_sha
   ```
1. [REQ-9.2] WHEN the worker runs a pending restack for a change that is no longer draft or open, THE parleyd SHALL remove the pending record and do nothing else
   → no version, no event and no branch move for that change; no pending record remains
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_queue_test.go, a table over the state B reaches before the worker runs {abandoned, landed}: runPending(); assert B's version number and head(B.source) are unchanged; assert no pending restack exists; assert no parley.change.restack event exists
   ```
1. [REQ-9.3] WHEN a pending restack is recorded for a change that already has one, THE parleyd SHALL replace the older record, so that one restack runs, onto the newest commit
   → one pending record for the change; after the worker runs, one new restack version whose base_sha is the newest head below
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_queue_test.go: B depends on A; with the worker stopped record two new versions of A one after the other; assert count(pending restacks for B) == 1; runPending(); assert B.version == 2; assert latest version of B has base_sha == A.head_sha
   ```
1. [REQ-9.4] IF the git command of a restack fails for a reason other than a conflict (it cannot be started, it exits with an error that is not a conflict, or the repository cannot be read), THEN THE parleyd SHALL change nothing; in the background keep the pending record, write one error log line and keep the worker and the server process running; in the manual call answer with an internal error
   → background: no version, no event, needs_restack unchanged, the pending record still present, a later pending restack of another change is still run; manual: HTTP 500 with error_type internal
   Check: unit
   - setup: a workspace whose bare repository was created with git init in t.TempDir(), with a main branch
   ```
   in internal/change/restack_queue_test.go and internal/change/restack_handler_test.go, with a gitrepo stub whose rebase returns a non-conflict error for B only: (background) amend A, which has dependants B and C; runPending(); assert B.version == 1; assert a pending restack for B exists; assert B.needs_restack == false; assert latest version of C has kind 'restack'; (manual) r = POST B/restack; assert r.status == 500; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'internal'; assert B.version == 1
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An agent amends the bottom of a three-change stack and the hub restacks the two above

1. **git client** pushes three branches to the workspace, each one commit on top of the previous
2. **agent** opens a change for each branch with POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes, bottom first
3. **parleyd** records version 1 of each change and links them: change 2 depends on change 1, change 3 on change 2
4. **git client** force-pushes the amended bottom branch
5. **parleyd** records version 2 of change 1 and a pending restack of change 2 in one transaction, and answers the push
6. **parleyd** replays change 2 onto the new head, moves its source branch, records a restack version and emits parley.change.version and parley.change.restack
7. **parleyd** does the same for change 3 onto the new head of change 2
8. **agent** reads GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/changes/3/stack and sees the three changes bottom first with needs_restack false
9. **git client** fetches the third branch and finds the amended bottom commit among its ancestors

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd HTTP server and router, git smart HTTP server, change store on a real SQLite file, internal/gitrepo running the git binary, restack worker, event log

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a data directory in t.TempDir()
- a ready workspace demo with a main branch and changes.auto_restack true
- a user with write access and an API key
- the git command on PATH

**End state:**

- changes 2 and 3 each have a version 2 of kind restack with created_by.actor_type system
- the hub's branch of change 3 has the amended bottom commit as an ancestor
- the stack route lists changes 1, 2, 3 in that order, each with needs_restack false
- the event log holds parley.change.restack for change 2 and then for change 3, both with trigger version

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/stack_restack_test.go: start the hub; git push branches a, b, c; open changes 1..3 over HTTP; assert GET changes/3 .depends_on == 2; amend a and git push --force; poll GET changes/3 until version == 2 (deadline 10 s); assert versions/2 of changes 2 and 3 have kind 'restack'; git fetch; assert git merge-base --is-ancestor <amended a> origin/c; s = GET changes/3/stack; assert numbers == [1, 2, 3] and every needs_restack == false; assert GET /events/log filtered to parley.change.restack lists change 2 then change 3
```

### PATH-2: A restack conflicts, the agent sees it as data and fixes it with a push

1. **git client** pushes two stacked branches that edit the same line of one file
2. **agent** opens a change for each branch
3. **git client** pushes a new commit to the lower branch that rewrites that line
4. **parleyd** tries to restack the upper change, hits a conflict, leaves its branch where it was, sets needs_restack with restack_reason conflict and the conflict report, and emits parley.change.conflict
5. **parley CLI** runs parley change restack for the upper change, prints the rebase_conflict envelope with the conflict report on stderr and exits 1
6. **git client** rebases the upper branch onto the new lower head, resolving the line, and force-pushes it
7. **parleyd** records the pushed version, finds the lower head among its ancestors and clears needs_restack
8. **parley CLI** runs parley change stack for the upper change and prints both changes with needs_restack false

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd HTTP server and router, git smart HTTP server, change store on a real SQLite file, internal/gitrepo running the git binary, restack worker, parley CLI binary code path with its HTTP client

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a data directory in t.TempDir()
- a ready workspace demo with a main branch and changes.auto_restack true
- a user with write access and an API key in PARLEY_API_KEY
- the git command on PATH

**End state:**

- after the conflicting push the upper change has version 1, needs_restack true, restack_reason conflict and a conflict report naming the file
- parley change restack exited 1 with error_type rebase_conflict on stderr and nothing on stdout
- after the fixing push the upper change has version 2 of kind push, needs_restack false and restack_reason null
- parley change stack exited 0 and printed two changes, lower first

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/stack_restack_test.go: start the hub; push a and b (b on a, both editing line 1 of f.txt); open changes 1 and 2; push a new commit on a rewriting line 1; poll GET changes/2 until needs_restack == true (deadline 10 s); assert restack_reason == 'conflict', version == 1, conflict.files[0].path == 'f.txt'; code, out, errOut = parley('change', 'restack', 'demo', '2'); assert code == 1 and out == '' and parse(errOut).error.error_type == 'rebase_conflict'; locally git rebase b onto a with the line resolved, git push --force; ch = GET changes/2; assert ch.version == 2 and ch.needs_restack == false and ch.restack_reason == null; code, out, _ = parley('change', 'stack', 'demo', '2'); assert code == 0 and numbers(parse(out).changes) == [1, 2]
```

## Dependencies

- `09` — builds its CLI commands on the client, output and exit-code helpers of the CLI foundation
- `23` — implements the Restacker interface its abandon calls, receives depends_on from its PATCH through the StackLinker of package 22, uses the caller rule of CHG-FR-020 and the function that stores mergeable with its conflict report, and through it the change record and version recording of package 22
- `52` — emits its hub events through the event log component

## Tasks

### 1. Link changes into stacks from the commit graph (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the behaviours of the automatic link, dependants and own-commit stats to internal/change/stack_test.go as table-driven tests over a repository made with git init in t.TempDir(), and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Use the fields depends_on, needs_restack and restack_reason that package 22 owns on the change record, through its setters; add only the commit a flagged change must sit on (the landed commit of the change that was below) as a column of this package's own, through a store migration
- 1.3 Add the link computation: among the other draft or open changes of the same workspace and target branch, keep those whose current head is a proper ancestor of the new head (ancestry asked of internal/gitrepo), take the one with the fewest commits to the new head, and the lowest number on a tie; a change with the same head, another target, another workspace or a closed state is never a candidate
- 1.4 Implement LinkVersion of the StackLinker interface that package 22 declares in internal/change/collaborators.go and register it: package 22 calls it inside its transaction for version 1 and for every later version; store depends_on through package 22's setter and set the version's base_sha to the lower change's head, or to the merge base with the target branch when there is no link, through package 22's setter for the base of the current version
- 1.5 Rely on that base setter to recompute stats, paths and the patch id from the commits after the new base_sha, so that a dependent change counts only its own commits
- 1.6 Leave dependants to package 22, which derives them from the stored links as the ascending numbers of the draft and open changes whose depends_on is the change; confirm it in the tests of this task
- 1.7 Use the source workspace's repository for the ancestry query when the source is a fork of the target workspace

### 4. Restack dependants in the background when the change below gets a new version (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4, REQ-9.3

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the behaviours of the pending records to internal/change/restack_queue_test.go and of the restack itself to internal/change/restack_test.go, with a runPending helper that runs the worker once, and confirm they fail
- 4.2 Add the pending restack record to the store: one per change (workspace, change number, trigger, and the landed commit where there is one), where recording another for the same change replaces it
- 4.3 From LinkVersion, which runs in the transaction of the version, record one pending restack with trigger version for each direct dependant of the change when the target workspace's setting changes.auto_restack is true; a failure to write it fails the whole transaction
- 4.4 Add the restack operation: read the dependant's source branch head; resolve the commit to sit on (the current head of the change named by depends_on, or the landed commit of the record); when the head already has that commit as an ancestor, end as up to date; otherwise replay the commits after the change's base_sha up to its head onto that commit with the rebase of internal/gitrepo, which changes no ref
- 4.5 Move the source branch to the replayed head with a compare-and-swap on the head that was read; when it is lost, start again from reading the head, at most 5 attempts in one run; after the fifth, end without changing anything and keep the pending record
- 4.6 Record the result through the version recording of package 22 (RecordVersion, in a store transaction of the restack that also holds the compare-and-swap result) as a version of kind restack: created_by with actor_type system and no creating credential, the session_id of the version it replaces, base_sha the commit sat on, patch_equivalent_to as package 22 computes it; clear needs_restack and restack_reason unless the reason is stack_too_deep
- 4.7 Emit parley.change.version (kind restack) and then parley.change.restack with onto_sha and the record's trigger through the event component, in the transaction of the version, with actor system and the dependant's ref, version and head_sha
- 4.8 Because the restack version goes through the same version recording, it records the pending restacks of the dependant's own dependants; check with a chain of four that the work runs bottom first
- 4.9 Add the worker: a goroutine started from internal/hub/change.go that is woken when a record is written, runs pending restacks one at a time per workspace in the order they were recorded, removes a record when its restack ends as restacked or up to date, and stops when the server's context is cancelled
- 4.10 Add a test hook on the restack operation between reading the head and the compare-and-swap, used only by the tests that move the branch in between
